## Project summary

### Project title and location

The proposed project is the **Harbor Point Heat and Stormwater Resilience Plan**, which sets out to reduce extreme-heat exposure and street flooding in Harbor Point between 2027 and 2032.

[Information needed: Confirm the country in which Harbor Point is located.]

### Delivery arrangements

The total programme cost is USD 26.5 million. Harbor Point will contribute USD 7.9 million from its capital budget, and the plan seeks USD 18.6 million in external grant funding.

title: Climate rationale and baseline
body_markdown:
## Climate rationale and baseline

### Extreme heat

Harbor Point recorded 23 days above 35 °C in 2025, compared with an average of 9 such days per year between 1991 and 2020. Heat-related emergency department visits rose from 140 in 2021 to 310 in 2025.

Eastside and Millbrook have the lowest tree canopy in the city, at 11 percent and 13 percent respectively.

### Stormwater flooding

Street flooding affects 37 intersections during a 10-year rainfall event. The Canal Street underpass closed 6 times in 2025 because of standing water.

The existing drainage network in Eastside was designed for a 5-year storm and is undersized for current rainfall intensities.

### Exposed people and assets

Harbor Point has 182,400 residents. The available evidence does not quantify the number of residents exposed to extreme heat or stormwater flooding.

[Information needed: Confirm the number of Harbor Point residents exposed to extreme heat or stormwater flooding.]

The documented assets affected by stormwater flooding include 37 intersections during a 10-year rainfall event and the Canal Street underpass.

### Without-project baseline

The evidence documents observed heat and flooding conditions but does not state expected conditions during the 2027–2032 plan period without the project.

[Information needed: Confirm the expected annual number of days above 35 °C in Harbor Point during the 2027–2032 plan period without the project.]

[Information needed: Confirm the expected number of Harbor Point intersections affected by street flooding during a 10-year rainfall event in the 2027–2032 plan period without the project.]

title: Project components and activities
body_markdown:
## Project components and activities

### Component 1: Cool corridors

The project will plant 4,800 street trees along 12 cool corridors connecting schools, clinics, and transit stops in Eastside and Millbrook. The Millbrook Neighbours Alliance will co-design cool corridor routes with residents. Cool corridor planting includes three years of establishment watering.

### Component 2: Green stormwater infrastructure

The project will build 85 bioretention cells and convert 3.2 hectares of asphalt schoolyards into permeable green play areas. Together, these measures are designed to capture the first 25 millimetres of rainfall from 41 hectares of impervious surface.

The Department of Public Works will deliver the green stormwater infrastructure, and the Harbor Point Unified School District will host the schoolyard conversions.

[Information needed: Confirm the locations of the 85 bioretention cells in Harbor Point.]

[Information needed: Confirm the locations of the schoolyards to be converted into 3.2 hectares of permeable green play areas in Harbor Point.]

### Component 3: Community cooling network

The Office of Climate Resilience will designate 18 community cooling centres in libraries and recreation centres, with extended opening hours on days above 32 °C.

[Information needed: Confirm the locations of the 18 community cooling centres in Harbor Point.]

title: Expected results and indicators
body_markdown:
## Expected results and indicators

### Expected results

The project will plant 4,800 street trees along 12 cool corridors in Eastside and Millbrook, build 85 bioretention cells, convert 3.2 hectares of asphalt schoolyards into permeable green play areas, and designate 18 community cooling centres in libraries and recreation centres.

The cool-corridor measures are intended to support a tree canopy target of 25 percent in both Eastside and Millbrook by 2032. The green stormwater measures are designed to capture the first 25 millimetres of rainfall from 41 hectares of impervious surface.

[Information needed: Confirm the intended direct-beneficiary population groups for the Harbor Point Heat and Stormwater Resilience Plan.]

[Information needed: Confirm the number of direct beneficiaries of the Harbor Point Heat and Stormwater Resilience Plan.]

### Monitoring and indicators

The Office of Climate Resilience will publish an annual progress report. The reported indicators will include tree canopy cover, the number of flooded intersections during monitored storms, and heat-related emergency department visits.

| Indicator | Baseline | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tree canopy cover in Eastside | 11 percent | 25 percent by 2032 |
| Tree canopy cover in Millbrook | 13 percent | 25 percent by 2032 |
| Number of flooded intersections during monitored storms | [Information needed: Confirm the baseline number of Harbor Point intersections flooded during monitored storms for the project monitoring indicator.] | [Information needed: Confirm the target number of Harbor Point intersections flooded during monitored storms for the project monitoring indicator.] |
| Heat-related emergency department visits | 310 in 2025 | [Information needed: Confirm the target number of heat-related emergency department visits in Harbor Point for the project monitoring indicator.] |

The available evidence records that street flooding affects 37 intersections during a 10-year rainfall event and that heat-related emergency department visits rose from 140 in 2021 to 310 in 2025. It does not establish a target reduction in flooded intersections or heat-related emergency department visits.

title: Implementation arrangements
body_markdown:
## Implementation arrangements

### Implementing entities and partner roles

The Office of Climate Resilience leads delivery together with the Department of Public Works. The Department of Public Works delivers green stormwater infrastructure.

The Office of Climate Resilience will designate 18 community cooling centres in libraries and recreation centres, with extended opening hours on days above 32 °C.

The Harbor Point Unified School District will host schoolyard conversions. The community organisation Millbrook Neighbours Alliance will co-design cool corridor routes with residents.

### Governance

The Harbor Point City Council adopted the Harbor Point Heat and Stormwater Resilience Plan on 14 March 2026.

[Information needed: Confirm the governance arrangement that will oversee implementation of the Harbor Point Heat and Stormwater Resilience Plan.]

### Monitoring and reporting

The Office of Climate Resilience will publish an annual progress report. Indicators will include tree canopy cover, the number of flooded intersections during monitored storms, and heat-related emergency department visits.

title: Indicative financing
body_markdown:
## Indicative financing

### Total cost and cost basis

The total programme cost is USD 26.5 million. The indicative cost allocation is USD 9.6 million for cool corridors, including planting and three years of establishment watering; USD 14.2 million for green stormwater infrastructure, including design and construction supervision; and USD 2.7 million for the community cooling network.

| Component | Indicative cost (USD million) | Cost basis |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Cool corridors | 9.6 | Planting and three years of establishment watering |
| Green stormwater infrastructure | 14.2 | Design and construction supervision |
| Community cooling network | 2.7 | [Information needed: Confirm the cost basis for the USD 2.7 million community cooling network allocation.] |
| **Total** | **26.5** |  |

### Co-financing

Harbor Point will contribute USD 7.9 million from its capital budget. The community cooling network, with an indicative cost of USD 2.7 million, is funded from the city operating budget.

[Information needed: Confirm whether the USD 2.7 million city operating-budget funding for the community cooling network is additional to, or included within, Harbor Point's USD 7.9 million capital-budget contribution.]
